article.title: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2026: Free Course on AI-Native Software Engineering
article.subtitle: Learn how to build, test, deploy, extend, and audit software with AI developer tools without losing engineering discipline.
article.description: Free AI Dev Tools course: build and ship a full-stack app with coding agents, MCP, and open-source AI security and DevOps tools. Earn a certificate.
article.notice: The 2026 materials are still being finalized. The repository shows the direction for the next cohort, but some videos, homework, deadlines, and module details may change before the course starts.
article.author: valeriiakuka

sections.title: Who the course is for
sections.body: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp is for developers and technical data professionals who want a repeatable, disciplined way of working with AI coding tools.

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.body: You don't need any prior experience with AI tools. You should have basic programming ability in Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, or a similar language; comfort using the command line; Git and GitHub basics; and willingness to read, review, debug, and maintain AI-generated code.

sections.title: Course curriculum
sections.body: Over four modules, you turn a vague idea into a specification and a groomed backlog, then build and deploy a full-stack application with AI assistance. After that you extend coding agents with MCP and reusable capabilities, and add safeguards to your project with open-source AI tools for security, audit, and DevOps.

sections.title: How to join
sections.body: You can join AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp either by following a live cohort or learning at your own pace.

aleksandrkim.name: Aleksandr Kim
aleksandrkim.bio: Aleksandr Kim is a Senior Data Scientist at Intuit, based in London - doing what most people outside the company would now call AI engineering: building AI-powered features in production at scale. About 9 years across banking (Raiffeisen), cybersecurity (Kaspersky), retail (X5 Retail Group), and fintech (Intuit), with experience on both sides of the IC–management line: I led two data science teams at X5 Retail Group before moving back to IC at Intuit, and I founded and run Intuit's 70+ member Data Science Guild. Inventor on 15+ ML/AI patents.

transcript.text: Today we are going to talk about AI engineering and what it takes to build AI in production along with all the glamorous work behind this. We have a special guest today named Aleksandr Kim. Aleksandr is a senior data scientist at Intuit. He is based in London doing what people usually describe as AI engineering. This is an overloaded term.

Although it seems in the industry we are slowly converging to some agreement on what AI engineering is maybe this is something we can talk about today too. He is doing exactly that he is doing AI engineering which means building AI powered features in production at scale. He has experience in banking cyber security retail and fintech across many companies. It is really nice to have you here Aleksandr. Welcome.
Thanks for the intro. Thanks for having me.

sections.title: Star the GitHub repository
sections.body: All course materials are here. Each module has its own folder (for example 01-overview, 03-mcp), and cohort-specific homework and deadlines are under the cohorts folder.

sections.title: Join the Slack channel
sections.body: After joining the DataTalks.Club Slack workspace, find the #course-ai-dev-tools-zoomcamp channel. This is where questions, announcements, and discussion happen.

sections.title: Follow the announcements
sections.body: Join the course Telegram channel. Subscribe to the DataTalks.Club YouTube channel and check the course playlist.

sections.title: How to work through the course
sections.body: Start with the Q&A or launch session and Module 1. Read the README in each module folder, watch the pre-recorded lectures, do the homework, finish the final project, and then review three peers' projects.

faq.question: How do I access the course modules and materials?
answer: All course materials are in the GitHub repo. Each module has its own folder (e.g. 01-overview, 03-mcp), and cohort-specific homework is under the cohorts/ folder.

Lectures are pre-recorded and available in the YouTube playlist. New workshops or updated videos are announced on Slack and Telegram. If you don't see an announcement, assume everything you need is already there.

Each homework has a strict deadline listed on the schedule; after the deadline the form closes. Submissions appear on the leaderboard. You can earn extra points by sharing your learning publicly with the hashtag #aidevtools and tagging Alexey Grigorev or DataTalksClub.

podwiki.title: AI Coding Tools
podwiki.summary: How Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code, notebook-to-agent workflows, and human review shape AI-generated code.
podwiki.lead: AI coding tools are assistants that sit in IDEs, terminals, and repositories. They use large language models to generate code, complete snippets, refactor files, and review diffs. Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and web-based prototyping tools like Lovable all belong here. These tools are now a practical part of AI Engineering and Software Engineering. They speed up prototypes and help developers move across stacks. They also make review discipline more important.
podwiki.boundary: Use the codebase as the boundary. Use this page when the assistant changes code, reads project files, or opens pull requests. It also fits prototypes that turn an idea into runnable code.
